blocks.explanation: Find the slope from the two points, use point-slope form, then rearrange into each required form.

blocks.explanation: \(p\) and the angle of the perpendicular are given: use the normal form \(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = p\).

book_ref.quote: is the perpendicular distance of the line from the origin and

blocks.final_answer: \(x - y + 4 = 0\); intercepts \(-4\) and \(4\); foot \((-2, 2)\) lies on the line.

blocks.prompt: 3 Prove that the linear equation \(ax + by + c = 0\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are not both zero, always represents a straight line. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Since \(a\), \(b\) are not both zero, only three cases are possible; reduce each to a known line.

book_ref.quote: represents a straight line, where

steps: Case I, \(a = 0\): then \(b \neq 0\) and \(by + c = 0 \Rightarrow y = -\dfrac{c}{b}\)
\(y\) has the same value at every point: a straight line parallel to the x-axis
Case II, \(b = 0\): then \(a \neq 0\) and \(ax + c = 0 \Rightarrow x = -\dfrac{c}{a}\), a straight line parallel to the y-axis
This is \(y = mx + k\) with slope \(m = -\dfrac{a}{b}\) and y-intercept \(k = -\dfrac{c}{b}\): a straight line
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(ax + by + c = 0\) always represents a straight line.

blocks.prompt: 4 Transform \(5x - 12y + 26 = 0\) into (i) slope-intercept form (ii) two-intercept form (iii) normal form (iv) point-slope form (v) two-point form (vi) symmetric form. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find the slope \(-\frac{a}{b}\) and the two intercepts first; every form is built from them.

book_ref.quote: Theorem 2: To transform the equation

blocks.prompt: 5 Prove that \(ax + by + c = 0\) can be reduced to the normal form \(\dfrac{ax + by}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} = \dfrac{-c}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\), the sign being chosen so that the right side is positive. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Compare with \(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = p\): equations of the same line have proportional coefficients.

book_ref.quote: If (i) and (iii) are identical, we must have

steps: Normal form: \(x\cos\theta + y\sin\theta = p\); given line: \(ax + by = -c\)
Substituting: \(\dfrac{ax + by}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}} = \dfrac{-c}{\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\); since \(p \ge 0\), the sign is chosen to make the right side positive
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: dividing \(ax + by = -c\) by \(\pm\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}\) (sign making the right side positive) gives the normal form, with \(p = \dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}}\).

blocks.prompt: 6 Transform the general equation \(ax + by + c = 0\) (\(a, b, c \neq 0\)) into (i) slope-intercept form (ii) point-slope form (iii) two-intercept form, and read off the slope and the intercepts. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Rearrange the equation until it looks exactly like each standard form, then read off the constants.

book_ref.quote: Each standard form shows one property of the line at a glance

steps: Put \(y = 0\): \(ax + c = 0\), \(x = -\dfrac{c}{a}\), so \(\left(-\dfrac{c}{a}, 0\right)\) lies on the line

blocks.prompt: 7 Triangle \(ABC\) has vertices \(A(-4, 1)\), \(B(2, 5)\), \(C(4, -3)\). Find the equations of its three medians and show that they are concurrent. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Mid-points of the sides, then each median through a vertex and a mid-point; finally test one common point in all three.

book_ref.quote: A median joins the vertex of a triangle to the mid-point of the opposite side.

blocks.prompt: 8 For the triangle \(A(-4, 1)\), \(B(2, 5)\), \(C(4, -3)\), find the equations of the altitudes and their point of concurrency. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: For each altitude: slope of the opposite side, negative reciprocal, point-slope form through the vertex.

book_ref.quote: An altitude is the line drawn from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

blocks.prompt: 9 For the triangle \(A(-4, 1)\), \(B(2, 5)\), \(C(4, -3)\), find the right bisectors of the sides, their common point \(O\), and show that \(O\) is equidistant from the vertices. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Each right bisector: through the mid-point of a side with the perpendicular slope.

book_ref.quote: A perpendicular or right bisector of a triangle is a line that is perpendicular to one side of the triangle

blocks.prompt: 10 Prove that three non-parallel lines \(a_ix + b_iy + c_i = 0\) (\(i = 1, 2, 3\)) are concurrent iff \(\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Find the meeting point of the first two lines and put it in the third.

book_ref.quote: Theorem 3: three non-parallel lines

steps: \(\ell_1 \nparallel \ell_2\), so \(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1 \neq 0\) and they meet at \(x = \dfrac{b_1c_2 - b_2c_1}{a_1b_2 - a_2b_1}\), \(y = \dfrac{a_2c_1 - a_1c_2}{a_1b_2 - a_2b_1}\)
The lines are concurrent iff this point lies on \(\ell_3\): \(a_3x + b_3y + c_3 = 0\)
Substitute and multiply by \(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1 \neq 0\): \(a_3(b_1c_2 - b_2c_1) + b_3(a_2c_1 - a_1c_2) + c_3(a_1b_2 - a_2b_1) = 0\)
This is the expansion of \(\begin{vmatrix} a_1 & b_1 & c_1 \\ a_2 & b_2 & c_2 \\ a_3 & b_3 & c_3 \end{vmatrix}\) along its third row
Every step can be reversed (we only multiplied by a non-zero number), so the condition is necessary and sufficient
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: the three non-parallel lines are concurrent iff the determinant of their coefficients is \(0\).

blocks.prompt: 11 Check whether the lines \(3x + y - 7 = 0\), \(x - 2y + 7 = 0\) and \(5x - 2y + 3 = 0\) are concurrent. If so, find the point of concurrency. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Theorem 3: evaluate the determinant of the coefficients; if it is zero, solve two of the lines.

book_ref.quote: the point of intersection of any two lines is the point of concurrency

steps: Slopes \(-3\), \(\dfrac{1}{2}\), \(\dfrac{5}{2}\) are different, so no two lines are parallel

blocks.explanation: Set the determinant of the coefficients equal to zero and solve for k; then solve the first two lines.

blocks.explanation: Write \(\ell_1 + k\ell_2 = 0\), find its slope in terms of \(k\), and use the slope condition.

book_ref.quote: One extra condition (parallel, perpendicular, through a point) fixes

steps: Check: the given lines meet at \((2, 2)\); \(8 - 2 - 6 = 0\) and \(2 + 8 - 10 = 0\)

blocks.prompt: 14 Prove that the altitudes of a triangle with vertices \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), \(C(x_3, y_3)\) are concurrent. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Write the three altitudes in general form, apply Theorem 3, and add rows 2 and 3 to row 1.

book_ref.quote: Altitudes of a triangle are concurrent.

steps: Slope of \(BC = \dfrac{y_2 - y_3}{x_2 - x_3}\), so the altitude from \(A\) is \(y - y_1 = -\dfrac{x_2 - x_3}{y_2 - y_3}(x - x_1)\)
Concurrent iff \(\begin{vmatrix} x_2 - x_3 & y_2 - y_3 & p_1 \\ x_3 - x_1 & y_3 - y_1 & p_2 \\ x_1 - x_2 & y_1 - y_2 & p_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\)
Add rows 2 and 3 to row 1: \((x_2 - x_3) + (x_3 - x_1) + (x_1 - x_2) = 0\), same for \(y\), and \(p_1 + p_2 + p_3 = 0\) (each \(x_ix_j\), \(y_iy_j\) occurs once with each sign)
The first row is \(0, 0, 0\), so the determinant is \(0\); the altitudes are not parallel (the sides are not), so Theorem 3 applies
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: the altitudes of a triangle are concurrent (at the orthocentre).

blocks.prompt: 15 Prove that the right bisectors of the sides of a triangle with vertices \(A(x_1, y_1)\), \(B(x_2, y_2)\), \(C(x_3, y_3)\) are concurrent. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Right bisector of each side through its mid-point; then Theorem 3 with the zero-row trick.

book_ref.quote: Right bisectors of a triangle are concurrent.

steps: Mid-point of \(BC\): \(\left(\dfrac{x_2 + x_3}{2}, \dfrac{y_2 + y_3}{2}\right)\); perpendicular slope \(-\dfrac{x_2 - x_3}{y_2 - y_3}\)
Right bisector: \(x(x_2 - x_3) + y(y_2 - y_3) + q_1 = 0\), \(q_1 = -\tfrac{1}{2}(y_2^{2} - y_3^{2}) - \tfrac{1}{2}(x_2^{2} - x_3^{2})\) (difference of squares)

By symmetry: rows \((x_3 - x_1, y_3 - y_1, q_2)\) and \((x_1 - x_2, y_1 - y_2, q_3)\); concurrent iff \(\begin{vmatrix} x_2 - x_3 & y_2 - y_3 & q_1 \\ x_3 - x_1 & y_3 - y_1 & q_2 \\ x_1 - x_2 & y_1 - y_2 & q_3 \end{vmatrix} = 0\)
Add rows 2 and 3 to row 1: columns 1 and 2 give \(0\); column 3: \(y_2^{2} - y_3^{2} + y_3^{2} - y_1^{2} + y_1^{2} - y_2^{2} = 0\), same for \(x^{2}\)
A zero row makes the determinant \(0\), so the right bisectors are concurrent
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: the right bisectors of a triangle are concurrent (at the circumcentre, equidistant from the vertices).

blocks.prompt: 16 Prove that the angle \(\theta\) from a line \(\ell_1\) of slope \(m_1\) to a line \(\ell_2\) of slope \(m_2\) is given by \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1m_2}\). Deduce the conditions for \(\ell_1 \parallel \ell_2\) and \(\ell_1 \perp \ell_2\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Use the inclinations \(\alpha_1\), \(\alpha_2\) of the two lines and the exterior angle of the triangle they make with the x-axis.

book_ref.quote: be two non-vertical lines such that they are not perpendicular to each other

steps: \(\alpha_2\) is an exterior angle of the triangle formed with the x-axis: \(\alpha_2 = \alpha_1 + \theta\), so \(\theta = \alpha_2 - \alpha_1\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_2 - m_1}{1 + m_1m_2}\); \(\ell_1 \parallel \ell_2 \Leftrightarrow m_1 = m_2\), \(\ell_1 \perp \ell_2 \Leftrightarrow m_1m_2 = -1\).

blocks.prompt: 17 Find the interior angles of the triangle with vertices \(P(-1, 0)\), \(Q(5, 2)\), \(R(1, 6)\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: \(P \to Q \to R\) is anticlockwise; at each vertex turn from the side to the next vertex to the side to the previous vertex (the 'to' slope first).

book_ref.quote: go round the vertices anticlockwise and measure each angle

blocks.prompt: 18 The angle from the line \(y = 2x + 1\) to the line \(y = mx + 3\) is \(45^\circ\). (i) Find \(m\). (ii) Find the angle from the second line to the first, and the acute angle between them. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Put \(\tan 45^\circ = 1\) in Theorem 7 with \(m_1 = 2\), \(m_2 = m\).

book_ref.quote: The 'to' slope comes first in the numerator.

steps: From the second line (slope \(-3\)) to the first (slope \(2\)): \(\tan\phi = \dfrac{2 - (-3)}{1 + (-3)(2)} = \dfrac{5}{-5} = -1\)
\(\phi = 180^\circ - 45^\circ = 135^\circ\); the acute angle between the lines is \(45^\circ\)

blocks.prompt: 19 Prove that the area of the triangle with vertices \(P(x_1, y_1)\), \(Q(x_2, y_2)\), \(R(x_3, y_3)\) is \(\dfrac{1}{2}[x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)]\) (taking \(x_1 < x_3 < x_2\), points above the x-axis). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Drop perpendiculars \(PL\), \(RM\), \(QN\) to the x-axis: triangle = trapezium \(PLMR\) + trapezium \(RMNQ\) \(-\) trapezium \(PLNQ\).

book_ref.quote: A trapezium is a quadrilateral having two parallel and two non-parallel sides.

steps: Parallel sides are the ordinates \(y_1, y_3, y_2\); widths \(LM = x_3 - x_1\), \(MN = x_2 - x_3\), \(LN = x_2 - x_1\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2}[x_1(y_2 - y_3) + x_2(y_3 - y_1) + x_3(y_1 - y_2)]\); the area is \(|\Delta|\).

blocks.prompt: 21 Prove that \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) (\(b \neq 0\)) represents a pair of lines through the origin which are real and distinct if \(h^{2} > ab\), coincident if \(h^{2} = ab\) and imaginary if \(h^{2} < ab\). (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Multiply by \(b\), complete the square in \(by + hx\), then use the difference of two squares.

book_ref.quote: represents a pair of lines through the origin. The lines are

steps: Difference of squares: \(\left(by + hx + x\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right)\left(by + hx - x\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0\)
So the lines are \(by + x\left(h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0\) and \(by + x\left(h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0\), both through \((0, 0)\)

\(h^{2} > ab\): real, non-zero root, two real distinct lines; \(h^{2} = ab\): root \(0\), the same line \(by + hx = 0\); \(h^{2} < ab\): root imaginary, imaginary lines meeting in the real point \((0, 0)\)
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: the equation is the pair \(by + x\left(h \pm \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0\) through the origin; real and distinct, coincident or imaginary as \(h^{2} >, =, < ab\).

blocks.prompt: 22 Find the lines represented by \(6x^{2} + xy - 2y^{2} = 0\) and the acute angle between them. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Check \(h^{2} > ab\), factorize, then use \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2} - ab}}{a + b}\).

book_ref.quote: If the middle term splits easily, factorize (fastest).

blocks.prompt: 23 Show that the angle \(\theta\) between the lines \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) is given by \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2} - ab}}{a + b}\). Deduce the conditions for the lines to be coincident and perpendicular. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Get the sum and product of the slopes from the two lines, then use the angle formula of 5.6.

book_ref.quote: Thus, equation (iv) gives angle between the lines represented by equation (i).

blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2} - ab}}{a + b}\); coincident iff \(h^{2} = ab\), perpendicular iff \(a + b = 0\).

blocks.prompt: 24 Find the joint equation of the lines through the origin perpendicular to the lines \(4x^{2} - 4xy - 3y^{2} = 0\). Show that the angle between the new pair equals the angle between the given pair. (5 marks)
blocks.explanation: Factorize to get the slopes, take negative reciprocals, multiply the new lines, then compare angles with formula (iv).

book_ref.quote: Perpendicular check without the formula:

steps: New pair: \(a = 3\), \(h = -2\), \(b = -4\): \(\tan\phi = \dfrac{2\sqrt{4 + 12}}{3 - 4} = -8\); the acute angle is \(\tan^{-1}8 \approx 82.87^\circ\) in both
blocks.final_answer: \(3x^{2} - 4xy - 4y^{2} = 0\); both pairs make the acute angle \(\tan^{-1}8 \approx 82.87^\circ\).
